name: Tienda en Regla
author: hojasclaras

sections.description:
En castellano: Tienda en Regla ayuda a las tiendas online argentinas con el BOTÓN DE ARREPENTIMIENTO y el BOTÓN DE BAJA DE SERVICIO (Disp. 954/2025), la verificación por pedido (Disp. 3/2026), los datos de atención al cliente y del vendedor, el Data Fiscal de ARCA, el aviso del derecho de revocación y el “PRECIO SIN IMPUESTOS NACIONALES”. La interfaz viene en castellano de Argentina: en los sitios configurados en Español de Argentina (es_AR), WordPress instala la traducción automáticamente; los nombres legales están siempre en castellano. Los datos de las solicitudes quedan en la base de datos de tu sitio: el autor del plugin no recibe ni ve ningún dato.

Tienda en Regla helps Argentine online stores with the consumer rules that apply to selling online. It works on any WordPress site that sells; with WooCommerce it adds order verification, order notes, product exclusions, notices and prices. The legal names (“BOTÓN DE ARREPENTIMIENTO”, “BOTÓN DE BAJA DE SERVICIO”, “PRECIO SIN IMPUESTOS NACIONALES”) are fixed in Spanish and cannot be edited, because the rules name them that way.

What it does, and which rule each part follows

Each line says the rule and the date the rule was last read in the official sources (InfoLeg, servicios.infoleg.gob.ar and argentina.gob.ar/normativa; and arca.gob.ar).

  • BOTÓN DE ARREPENTIMIENTO (withdrawal button): a thin bar fixed at the top of every page by default, plus an optional floating button, menu item, block, shortcode and widget. The form works without an account or login, shows the request code on screen at once and sends it by email. – Disposición SSDCyLC 954/2025 (Boletín Oficial 4-Sep-2025), arts. 1, 3 and 5; Ley 24.240 art. 34; Código Civil y Comercial (CCyC) arts. 1110 to 1116. Reviewed 2026-10-13.
  • BOTÓN DE BAJA DE SERVICIO (service cancellation button): same form for cancelling a service. Off by default; the setup wizard asks whether you sell services, and showing it always is the most prudent option. The merchant notice reminds you of the free proof of cancellation within 72 hours. – Disp. 954/2025 art. 4; Ley 24.240 arts. 10 ter and 10 quáter. Reviewed 2026-10-13.
  • Verification by order (WooCommerce): the customer types the order number and the purchase email; if they match, the request is marked “verified” and linked to the order. A request that does not match is still registered and gets a code: the plugin never rejects a request. – Disposición DNDCyAC 3/2026 (Boletín Oficial 6-Feb-2026), art. 1. Reviewed 2026-10-13.
  • Indicative 10-day deadline: 10 calendar days from the later of the purchase and the delivery; the starting day is not counted; if the last day is a weekend or a holiday you load, it moves to the next business day. Shown only to the merchant, as a guide. – Ley 24.240 art. 34; CCyC arts. 6 and 1110. Art. 1110 reviewed 2026-10-13, art. 6 reviewed 2026-10-15.
  • Notice of the right of withdrawal: in WooCommerce order emails to the customer (in the order details area, woocommerce_email_order_meta, not in the email footer), on the “order received” page, and in the checkout (classic and block checkout; in the block checkout it appears in the order summary as text, without adding any field). Each place can be turned off. – Ley 24.240 art. 34; CCyC art. 1111. Reviewed 2026-10-13.
  • Products excluded from withdrawal (WooCommerce): mark a product or a category with the exception that applies; a line on the product page tells the customer. The withdrawal button stays visible. – CCyC art. 1116; Disp. 954/2025 art. 3. Reviewed 2026-10-13.
  • Customer service: phone, email, WhatsApp, contact page, responsible area and hours, in the footer or as a block, with a check for the 8-hour minimum when service is only by phone or electronic means. – Disp. 954/2025 art. 6. Reviewed 2026-10-13.
  • Seller details: name, address and CUIT in the footer or as a block, with a warning if the address looks like a post office box. – Ley 24.240 arts. 8 and 33. Reviewed 2026-10-13.
  • Data Fiscal: paste the code that ARCA gives you; the plugin keeps only the link to ARCA and shows it, around the official Data Fiscal logo that ships with the plugin (an unmodified copy of ARCA’s image), in the footer or as a block. It never draws a QR or a logo of its own, and it loads nothing from other servers. It reminds you to replace the code if your site address changes. – Resolución General AFIP 1415/2003, arts. 24 to 26 (text of RG 4042-E/2017). Reviewed 2026-10-13.
  • “PRECIO SIN IMPUESTOS NACIONALES” (WooCommerce): a smaller line under the final price on product pages and product lists. See “How the price without national taxes is calculated” below. – Resolución SIC 4/2025 (Boletín Oficial 17-Jan-2025), art. 2 c. Reviewed 2026-10-13.
  • Personal data notice under the form, built from your seller details: purpose, recipients, controller, required fields, consequences and how to ask for access, rectification or deletion. – Ley 25.326 art. 6. Reviewed 2026-10-13 (arts. 14 to 16 on 2026-10-15).
  • Requests panel: list with filters and search, detail with status changes, delivery date and internal notes (each change is written in the notes with date and user), a link to the WooCommerce order and a “Go to refund” button that only opens WooCommerce’s own refund form. Shop managers can handle requests; only administrators see the settings.

Before each new version the rules are checked again in InfoLeg (“normas que modifican” of Disp. 954/2025 and Res. SIC 4/2025). Resolución 424/2020 is mentioned only as a repealed precedent: Disp. 954/2025 repealed it on 4-Sep-2025.

Merchant responsibility

The plugin helps you comply; it does not comply for you, and legal responsibility stays with the merchant. You decide each request, you make the refund (the plugin never refunds by itself), you send the proof of cancellation that Ley 24.240 art. 10 ter asks for, and you check that the tax rates, the seller details and the Data Fiscal code you enter are right. The deadline shown is only a guide. The plugin covers the documents that WordPress and WooCommerce make; invoices, delivery notes or emails from other systems are not covered. This plugin is not legal advice.

Where the withdrawal notice appears (WooCommerce)

  • Order emails to the customer: through woocommerce_email_order_meta, so it sits with the order details and works with themes that change the email footer.
  • “Order received” page: before the order details.
  • Classic checkout: just before the “Place order” button.
  • Block checkout: through the ExperimentalOrderMeta slot that WooCommerce documents for extensions. WooCommerce marks that slot as Experimental, so a future WooCommerce version could rename or move it; if that happens, the notice would stop showing in the block checkout (the checkout keeps working) until the plugin is updated. Tested with WooCommerce 11.2.

How the price without national taxes is calculated

The line shows: final price ÷ (1 + VAT rate + other national indirect taxes rate), using the rates you enter in Tienda en Regla > Prices and notices (default VAT 21 %, other taxes 0 %). For products on sale it uses the sale price; for variable products, the range (calculated with the tax class of the main product: if your variations have different tax classes, the line can differ from the range WooCommerce shows). It uses your store’s currency format. It is not shown next to instalment prices or unit prices (Res. SIC 4/2025 art. 2 d and e exempt them); if a payment plugin prints instalments next to the price, turn the line off with the tenreg_show_net_price filter. Checking that the rate is right for each product is the merchant’s responsibility; the free plugin uses one rate for the whole store.

Multisite

Supported in the code (network activation prepares every site, new sites too; deleting a site deletes its table; each site is an independent store with its own panel), but tested only on single sites. If you use it on a network, test it on a staging copy first.

External services

The plugin does not contact any server by itself: no calls from your server, no analytics, no updates or licence checks, and every image, script and style it uses is served from your own site. Two links on your public pages take the visitor to a third party when clicked, and only if you set them up:

ARCA (Agencia de Recaudación y Control Aduanero, Argentina) – Data Fiscal. Only if you paste your Data Fiscal code. The Data Fiscal logo is served from your site (the plugin ships an unmodified copy of ARCA’s image in assets/img/data-fiscal.jpg), so loading your pages sends nothing to ARCA. The link takes the visitor to ARCA’s page for your business only when the visitor clicks it; then ARCA receives the visitor’s request for that address, which identifies your business (that is what the link is for). The plugin itself sends nothing to ARCA, and no data from the requests is sent. Showing this link is required by RG AFIP 1415/2003 art. 25. Service: https://www.arca.gob.ar/960/ . ARCA’s home page does not link a privacy policy that the plugin author could find; its general site is https://www.arca.gob.ar/ .

WhatsApp (WhatsApp LLC) – contact link. Only if you enter a WhatsApp number in the customer service details. The footer and the block show a https://wa.me/<number> link. Nothing is loaded until a visitor clicks it; clicking opens WhatsApp with your number. Terms: https://www.whatsapp.com/legal/terms-of-service . Privacy policy: https://www.whatsapp.com/legal/privacy-policy .

Privacy

  • What is stored: for each request, the name, email, request type and code, dates and status; with WooCommerce, the order number and the link to the order; and only if the customer fills them in, the purchase date (sites without WooCommerce), products to return, reason, phone and DNI/CUIT (the phone and DNI/CUIT fields are off by default). Internal notes written by the store are stored too. The IP address is not stored: the anti-spam limit uses a keyed hash in a WordPress transient that expires within one hour.
  • Where: in a table of your own site’s database ({prefix}tenreg_solicitudes), not in posts, so it does not appear in searches, feeds or the public REST API. With WooCommerce, the order also gets a note and the last request code as order metadata.
  • Who sees it: administrators and, with WooCommerce, shop managers. The plugin author does not receive or see any data of your customers or of your store: there is no author server, no analytics and no third parties.
  • How long: 3 years after the request is closed by default (Ley 24.240 art. 50: sanctions prescribe in 3 years), configurable from 1 to 10 years; a request that was never closed counts from its last change. A daily task deletes what has expired.
  • Export: Tools > Export Personal Data includes the customer’s requests, internal notes included.
  • Erase: Tools > Erase Personal Data anonymizes by default the requests still inside the retention period: it empties the name, email, phone, DNI/CUIT, order number, products, reason and notes, and keeps only the code, type, status, dates, “verified” and the link to the order, as evidence of how the request was answered; WordPress is told that something was retained, with the reason. An anonymized request takes no new notes. Requests past the retention period are deleted. A setting (“Delete the requests instead of anonymizing them”) makes it always delete.
  • The order link, honestly: with WooCommerce, an anonymized request keeps its link to the order, and the order keeps a note with the request code. While the WooCommerce order still holds the customer’s data, the request can be related to that person through the order (strictly, that is pseudonymization, not anonymization). The order data is handled by WooCommerce’s own eraser (and its settings in WooCommerce > Settings > Accounts & Privacy), not by this plugin. If you prefer that the plugin keep nothing of the request, tick “Delete the requests instead of anonymizing them” (the order note with the code stays in the order).
  • Privacy policy: the plugin suggests a paragraph in Settings > Privacy > Policy guide, with your retention years. Review it and adapt it: your privacy policy is your responsibility.
  • Uninstall: deletes the settings and moves the two pages to the trash; the requests table is deleted only if you ticked “Delete all requests when the plugin is deleted”.
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins > Add New, search for “Tienda en Regla”, install and activate it. Or upload the zip in Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
  2. On activation the plugin creates the pages “BOTÓN DE ARREPENTIMIENTO” and “BOTÓN DE BAJA DE SERVICIO” and turns on the top bar.
  3. Answer the three questions of the setup wizard (Tienda en Regla > Setup wizard): whether you sell services, your seller details and the email for new requests.
  4. Fill in Tienda en Regla > Customer service and seller, and paste your Data Fiscal code in Tienda en Regla > Data Fiscal.
  5. With WooCommerce: review Tienda en Regla > Prices and notices (tax rates, where the withdrawal notice appears) and mark excluded products in the “Advanced” tab of each product, if any.
sections.faq:
Does it work without WooCommerce?

Yes. The buttons, the form, the codes, the emails, customer service, seller details and Data Fiscal work on any WordPress site. Verification by order, order notes, exclusions, the withdrawal notice and the price line need WooCommerce 9.0 or later.

Can I change the button text?

No. Disp. 954/2025 names the link “BOTÓN DE ARREPENTIMIENTO” (and “BOTÓN DE BAJA DE SERVICIO”), so the plugin uses those exact names in every language.

Does the plugin reject requests that arrive late or that do not match an order?

Never. Every request is registered and gets a code. The deadline and the verification are information for you; you decide.

Does it make the refund?

No. “Go to refund” opens WooCommerce’s own refund form in the order; you choose the items and the amount. Return costs are paid by the seller (Ley 24.240 art. 34).

My site caches whole pages. Does the form still work?

Yes. The form asks the server for a fresh security token when it is sent, so a cached page does not break it. Without JavaScript it also works: the form is shown again with a new token.

Do I have to show the BOTÓN DE BAJA DE SERVICIO if I only sell products?

The rule does not settle it (Disp. 954/2025 art. 4 refers to “la baja del servicio contratado”). It is off by default and the wizard asks; showing it always is the most prudent option.

Is the plugin translated?

The interface is in English. Translations come from translate.wordpress.org and WordPress installs them automatically; the Spanish (Argentina) translation is being contributed there. The legal names and the buttons are always in Spanish, as the rules require.

Where are the hooks for developers?

Filters: tenreg_find_order (custom order numbers), tenreg_requests_capability (who handles requests), tenreg_ip_rate_limit (requests per hour per network address), tenreg_show_net_price (turn the price line off for a product).
sections.changelog:
1.0.3

  • Fixed: the Data Fiscal logo was shown too large on WooCommerce pages.

1.0.2

  • The Data Fiscal logo is now served from the plugin’s own files (an unmodified copy of ARCA’s image); nothing is loaded from remote servers.

1.0.1

  • Output escaping hardened.
  • Translations now come from translate.wordpress.org (bundled files removed).
  • Admin notices shown only on the dashboard and the plugin’s own screens.

1.0.0

  • First public version.
  • BOTÓN DE ARREPENTIMIENTO and BOTÓN DE BAJA DE SERVICIO: top bar, floating button, menu item, 6 blocks, 5 shortcodes and a widget; form without login, request code on screen and by email, anti-spam without third parties, personal data notice.
  • Requests panel: list, filters, search, detail, status changes, delivery date, internal notes, 24-hour reminder on the Dashboard.
  • WooCommerce: verification by order, order note and box with “Go to refund” (HPOS on and off), WooCommerce emails, exclusions (CCyC art. 1116), withdrawal notice in emails, order received page and classic and block checkout, “PRECIO SIN IMPUESTOS NACIONALES”.
  • Customer service, seller details and Data Fiscal in the footer or as blocks; setup wizard.
  • WordPress privacy tools: exporter, eraser that anonymizes by default, suggested privacy policy text.
  • Multisite support (tested only on single sites).
  • Spanish (Argentina) translation included.
